data.hypothesis: The previous candidate’s combined target-mass cancellation and unrefined rsqrt-based inverse cube failed one large-N correctness case. Refining rsqrtf once and restoring the baseline’s mass-scaled accumulation and final division may reduce numerical deviation while retaining a faster reciprocal-distance calculation.

memory_lessons.applicability: Float32 accumulation differences can become visible at the largest tested size; approximate reciprocal arithmetic and target-mass cancellation should not be combined without separate validation.
memory_lessons.claim: The first integrated arithmetic candidate passed the smaller checks but failed one N=16384 correctness case with a reported maximum absolute error of 0.0003108978. No timing was recorded.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Refine rsqrtf with one Newton step and retain the baseline force scaling and final target-mass division; rerun the full checker before timing.

data.notes: This is a new correctness-oriented arithmetic experiment based on baseline-e1, not a reuse of the failed candidate as a measured source. It keeps src/launch.json unchanged. The previous candidate had no timing because correctness failed; this candidate is also unvalidated until the controller checks and measures it.
transformations: Cache the output particle state in a local value and continue writing a complete output record with its mass copied unchanged.
Use rsqrtf followed by one Newton refinement step, then form the inverse-distance cube with multiplications.
Restore the baseline’s target-mass-scaled force accumulation and velocity division to isolate the reciprocal-square-root change from target-mass cancellation.
Keep the launch configuration, softening, self-interaction skip, float32 accumulations, and velocity-before-position update order unchanged.
